classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Use the identity principle for analytic functions. Show that the zero set of `f` is closed and open in `U`, leveraging preconnectedness to conclude `f` is identically zero on `U`.
classifier_payload.theorem_statement: Let `𝕜` be a nontrivially normed field, and let `E` and `F` be normed spaces over the same field `𝕜`, with `F` complete. Let `U` be a preconnected subset of `E` and let `f : E → F` be analytic in a neighborhood of every point of `U`. Assume there is a point of `U` near which `f` agrees with the constant zero function. Show that `f` agrees with the constant zero function throughout `U`.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Let \(Z\subseteq U\) be the points near which \(f=0\). It is open. Use continuity of all derivatives and uniqueness of convergent analytic expansions to show \(Z\) is relatively closed: derivatives vanish at limit points, hence their Taylor series is zero. Preconnectedness then gives \(Z=U\).

Show that `f` agrees with the constant zero function throughout `U`.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Leverage the fact that `T` is an endomorphism of a torsion-free module over a domain. Use the properties of generalized eigenspaces and the distinctness of `λ` and `μ` to show that their respective generalized eigenspaces at any depths `k` and `l` must be disjoint.
classifier_payload.theorem_statement: Let `T` be an endomorphism of a torsion-free module over a domain, and let `λ` and `μ` be distinct scalars. For any generalized-eigenspace depths `k` and `l` in the extended natural numbers `ℕ∞` — including the unbounded depth — show that the generalized eigenspace of `T` for `λ` at depth `k` and the generalized eigenspace for `μ` at depth `l` have trivial intersection.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Reduce unbounded depths pointwise to finite exponents. Use the resultant identity for \((X-\lambda)^k\) and \((X-\mu)^l\) to show that a nonzero power of \(\lambda-\mu\) annihilates any common vector. Torsion-freeness then forces that vector to vanish.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Use the definition of linear independence and the properties of disjoint sums to show that the linear independence of the whole family is equivalent to the linear independence of the restrictions and the disjointness of their spans.
classifier_payload.theorem_statement: Let `v` be a family of vectors indexed by the disjoint sum of two index types. Show that the whole family is linearly independent if and only if the restriction to each side is linearly independent and the submodules spanned by the ranges of the two restrictions are disjoint.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Decompose every finitely supported coefficient function on the disjoint union into its two components. A vanishing total combination gives equal vectors in the two spans; disjointness forces both to vanish, and independence of each restriction kills all coefficients. Reverse implications follow by restriction and span-intersection witnesses.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Use compactness theorem in first-order logic. Represent graphs as structures and homomorphisms as interpretations. Show that the set of sentences asserting existence of homomorphisms from finite subgraphs to `F` is finitely satisfiable, hence satisfiable, implying a homomorphism from `G` to `F`.
classifier_payload.theorem_statement: Let `G` and `F` be graphs, with the vertex type of `F` finite. Assume that every subgraph of `G` having finitely many vertices admits a graph homomorphism into `F`. Show that there exists a graph homomorphism from all of `G` into `F`.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Use compactness: view vertex maps as points of the compact product \(V(F)^{V(G)}\). For each edge of \(G\), impose the closed homomorphism constraint. Finite subgraphs guarantee the finite-intersection property; hence all constraints have a common solution.
classifier_payload.theorem_statement: Let `G` and `F` be graphs, with the vertex type of `F` finite. Assume that every subgraph of `G` having finitely many vertices admits a graph homomorphism into `F`. Show that there exists a graph homomorphism from all of `G` into `F`.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Use the given assumption to iteratively join branches, ensuring finite steps to a common descendant. Prove by induction on the number of steps from the common start.
classifier_payload.theorem_statement: Let `r` be a reduction relation. Assume that whenever one object makes two direct `r`-steps to two successors, the branches can be joined so that one successor needs at most one further `r`-step and the other needs only finitely many `r`-steps. Show that whenever two objects are each reachable from a common start by finitely many `r`-steps, the two endpoints have a common descendant reachable from each by finitely many `r`-steps. Zero-step reachability is allowed.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Use a finite diagram-tiling argument. First prove a strip lemma: commute one reduction step across any finite reduction path by inductively filling local peaks, propagating the “at most one step” edge. Then induct on the other path; the grid’s opposite corner is the common descendant.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Use the fact that the product of measurable spaces is measurable. Show that the preimage of a measurable set under a coordinate-restriction map is measurable. Use the countable additivity of the measure to show that the preimage of a countable union of measurable sets is measurable.
classifier_payload.theorem_statement: Let a family of measurable spaces be indexed by an arbitrary type, and let `s` be a measurable subset of their product. Show that there is a countable set of coordinates `I` and a subset `t` of the product restricted to `I` such that `s` is exactly the preimage of `t` under the coordinate-restriction map. Thus membership in `s` depends only on the coordinates in `I`.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Show countably determined subsets form a σ-algebra: complements preserve coordinates, while countable unions use the countable union of coordinate sets. It contains every finite-coordinate cylinder generating the product σ-algebra. Hence \(s\) is determined by countable \(I\); define \(t\) from the resulting coordinate-equivalence classes.

Show that there is a countable set of coordinates `I` and a subset `t` of the product restricted to `I` such that `s` is exactly the preimage of `t` under the coordinate-restriction map. classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Use the orbit-stabilizer theorem, which states that the size of the orbit of an element is equal to the index of its stabilizer in the group. Organize the proof by showing that the action of the group partitions the set into disjoint orbits, and then applying the theorem to each orbit.
classifier_payload.theorem_statement: Let a finite group `G` act on a set and let `x` be a point. Show that the cardinality of the orbit of `x` multiplied by the cardinality of the stabilizer of `x` equals the cardinality of `G`.

classifier_payload.candidate_guidance: Use the map \(G\to Gx\), \(g\mapsto g\cdot x\). Show each fiber is a left coset of the stabilizer \(G_x\), hence has size \(|G_x|\). These fibers partition finite \(G\), one for each orbit point, yielding the desired product.
